# Coaching AI collaboration

## Patterns to recognize

| Pattern | What you observe | What may be happening | Try asking |
|---------|------------------|----------------------|------------|
| Hiding use | Polish, vague "I used AI a bit", can't explain reasoning | Shame, fear, or Accepting without awareness | Walk me through your process — where did *you* decide? |
| Receipts only | Long prompt logs, no reflection | Documentation mistaken for engagement | Where did you disagree or learn something new? |
| Avoiding AI | Struggle on tasks AI could scaffold | AI seen as cheating or threatening | What if AI challenged your ideas instead of writing them? |
| Growing collaboration | Dialogue trail; can separate contributions | This is what we want | What made you push back on X? |
| Regressing under pressure | Early Integrating, late Accepting when rushed | Deadlines; human, but needs noticing | What happened? How might you handle that differently next time? |
| Outsourcing the thinking | Polished portfolio or report; cannot recall or explain own text after time away | Accepting at scale — deliverable done, learning skipped | What do you still own? What would recovery look like (messy notes first, AI as memory not author)? |

See also the [portfolio story](ai.augmented.learning.portfolio.qmd) and [notes-first section](ai.augmented.learning.notes-first.qmd) — encoding while you listen matters as much as who polishes the final text.

## Growth is messy

A realistic trajectory — not a straight line:

- Week 2: Integrating (excited, experimenting)
- Week 4: Accepting (deadline pressure)
- Week 6: Challenging (feedback landed)
- Week 8: Accepting (project chaos)
- Week 10: Integrating (breakthrough)
- Week 14: Integrating (pulled it together)

What matters: Can they **notice** slipping into Accepting when higher engagement is needed? **Recover** when the task demands it? **Articulate** what they learned?

## What "proficient" looks like

A proficient learner (student or professional):

- Knows the difference between Accepting and Integrating
- Chooses consciously based on the task
- Documents process — not only prompts
- Explains what they learned vs what AI contributed
- Reflects honestly on shortcuts

They do not need to be brilliant at prompting. They need to be **in the driver's seat**.

## Proficiency scale (LO6)

| Scale | What it looks like |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Undefined** | No evidence of collaboration; avoids or hides use; cannot discuss process |
| **Orienting** | Uses AI without awareness; mostly Accepting; "I used ChatGPT" is the whole reflection |
| **Beginning** | Developing awareness; occasional Challenging or Integrating; starting to notice patterns |
| **Proficient** | Consistent conscious choice; articulates why; integrates when needed; honest about shortcuts |
| **Advanced** | Sophisticated integration; models practice for others; connects collaboration to societal impact |

## LO6 alongside other outcomes

LO6 is judged **in context** with the rest of the minor — same idea applies in professional teams:

| Focus | LO6 shows up as… |
|-------|------------------|
| Societal impact | Did AI widen perspectives — or narrow them? |
| Needs analysis | Verified suggestions — or accepted the first list? |
| Model interaction | Challenged outputs when building with AI? |
| Professional standard | How was AI used in stakeholder communication? |
| Personal leadership | Can they reflect on their own AI patterns? |

## Coaches: learn alongside

Most of us are still at a basic level with our own AI use. That is okay.

We have judged students for technologies we did not yet understand — calculators, Wikipedia, Google, Stack Overflow. Each time the tool became normal; each time we eventually taught **how to use it well** instead of **whether to use it at all**.

AI is this generation's moment. The invitation: **learn alongside your students**. Notice your own patterns. Curiosity models exactly what we ask of them.
